{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The doors closed without a sound. Mara counted the dry seats again: one for Lina, one for Kit, one for herself. Beyond them, every seat was wet.

“Don’t sit yet,” the driver said from the bridge.

At the wheel, the dripping shape lifted one hand. Water streamed from its sleeve, but no fingers showed beneath it. The bus began to move.

The real driver ran alongside, keeping one hand on the window. In the other he carried the upside-down bowl. He had left the key trapped on the bridge.

“You said places,” Mara called through the glass.

“Yes. Tell me how many.”

“Three dry seats. One at the wheel.”

Lina pointed to the folded napkins. “And four at the table.”

For an instant, the bus smelled of bread. Mara understood why the napkins had been set out. She snatched them from the seats and passed one to each of the others. Under the last napkin lay a small, round hole in the upholstery. From it came the sound of the river.

Across the water, Gran raised her hand. One finger.

Mara pressed the fourth napkin over the hole. The bus lurched. The shape at the wheel turned its head, and its face was a dark window looking into the tiny kitchen. There, the fourth chair stood empty.

“Sit,” the driver shouted.

They dropped into the three dry seats. The bus rolled on, and the driver fell away into the mist. Beneath Mara’s palm, the napkin stirred. Something on the other side knocked once."}
